what: Inspector bound-to-CMS caption, new text opens '🔗 chip in the header; bound fields go read-only with the collection and field named, plus an unbind action. A field that silently refuses typing is a bug report.'
finding: Nothing is read-only. No inspector control and no canvas path checks bindings, so a bound field accepts typing and the next content refresh silently takes it back — the caption's own 'a field that silently refuses typing is a bug report' inverts the actual failure. The chip is also not an emoji.
evidence: ProInspector.tsx:396 renders <Link size={10}/> plus the word 'Bound' in a bordered chip (:390-397) — a Lucide icon, not 🔗. boundLabel is consumed only by that chip; no control is disabled. useCanvasInlineEdit.ts:116 sets el.contentEditable='true' with no binding guard. BindingBanner.tsx:7 docstring: 'Typing into the canvas produced a change that the next content refresh silently took back'; ProInspector.tsx:475-476 calls them 'the controls that no longer decide anything'. The two appended facts (draft binding publishes, publish does not refresh canvas) are both TRUE — CMSBindingManager.ts:114-117 passes filter:{} with no status, ExportEngine.ts:701 mode 'static', exportPublishPages.ts:38 passes no cmsMode; CollectionManager.ts:317-322 emits CMS_CONTENT_PUBLISHED and CMSBindingManager.ts:75-77 / useCMSPreview.ts:123-124 subscribe only to created/updated/deleted.
fix: A 'Bound' chip (Lucide link icon) in the header; the banner names the collection and field and offers Unbind — but nothing below it is read-only. Typing here or on the canvas is accepted and silently reverted on the next content refresh. Two more things this state does not say: a binding to a DRAFT record publishes that draft's text, and publishing a record does not refresh the canvas.

what: AI governing note rewritten to 'AI proposes a diff for anything you ask it to change — alt text for a new image is the one exception, written automatically.'
finding: 'The one exception' is false. There is a second automatic AI write with no diff and no Apply: 'Write with AI' on the SEO tab commits an AI-generated page title straight into the field. Alt-text regeneration on an existing asset is a third.
evidence: SeoTab.tsx:197 'Write with AI' button -> :53-67 suggestTitle -> :61 `if (clean) s.setSeoTitle(clean);` — no proposal, no Apply. AssetDetailOverlay.tsx:281 `void onUpdate?.(item.key, { altText: clean });` regenerates on an existing asset, outside 'a new image'. The alt-text auto-trigger itself is TRUE (useAltTextAutoTrigger.ts:76 subscribes MEDIA_EVENTS.UPLOAD_COMPLETE, :64 composer.media.updateAsset; mounted StudioPanels.tsx:197). The undo half is TRUE (applySetStyle.ts:642 one beginTransaction per applyAiEdit; useAgentRunner.ts:280 one call per approved step) — though useAgentRunner.ts:177 auto-apply mode skips per-step approval.
fix: AI proposes a diff for anything you ask it to change — except two writes that land straight away: alt text for a new image, and 'Write with AI' on a page's SEO title. Each Apply lands as one undo step; a multi-step draft applies one step at a time, unless auto-apply is on.

what: Content fields caption rewritten to 'Deleting a field strips its values from every record and silently blanks every element bound to it — nothing can count those.'
finding: Deleting a field does not touch a single record. It rewrites collection.fields and saves the collection row; the values sit orphaned in item.data until that record is next saved. 'Strips its values from every record' is a positive claim about data mutation that the code does not make.
evidence: CollectionManager.ts:225-228 `const updatedFields = collection.fields.filter(f => f.id !== fieldId); await this.updateCollection(collectionId, { fields: updatedFields });` and updateCollection:141-147 writes only Storage.saveCollection. No content item is read or written. Values drop only when ContentViews.tsx:283 rebuilds `base` from collection.fields on the next save. The other two clauses ARE true: CMSBindingManager.ts:131-134 returns '' with no signal; BaseBindingManager.ts:72 keys bindings by elementId and exposes only getBindings(elementId) — no by-field or by-collection lookup. NOTE: the product's own confirm copy repeats the same false claim (ContentViews.tsx:577).
fix: The schema, not the data. Deleting a field hides its values rather than deleting them — every record keeps them until it is next saved — and silently blanks every element bound to it. Nothing can count those. (The confirm dialog's 'and its values on every record will be removed' is wrong too.)

what: Layers loading caption rewritten to '... The count is a skeleton, not a number: a count of a list that has not loaded is not a fact.'
finding: The footer is not a skeleton. It renders the literal text '0 layers' for the whole load. The caption states as fact the very thing the tab failed to do, and the previous finding (which said it reads '0 layers') was right.
evidence: LayersTab.tsx:216-222 — the footer is gated on `!treeFailed` only, never on projectLoading; treeFailed is set by LayersTreeBoundary which mounts only in the loaded branch (:194-207), so during load it is false and stats.total is 0 (initialised :113). Renders `${stats.total} layer${stats.total === 1 ? '' : 's'}`. LayersLoadingSkeleton (:209) lives inside .bdc-pbody only. The toolbar half IS true: toolbar at :159-185 sits outside the loading gate at :194, and its ⊞/⊟ emit 'layers:expand-all'/'layers:collapse-all' whose only listeners register in the unmounted panel (index.tsx:49-59).
fix: Tree fetching. The toolbar stays for position, not for use — its controls talk to the panel that has not mounted. The footer keeps counting: it reads '0 layers' for the whole load, which is not a count of anything.

what: Restore caption rewritten to 'Restore always confirms and always saves the current state as a version first. It replaces pages, styles and brand settings; content records, media and saved components are untouched.'
finding: Two problems. 'Always confirms' holds only for the versions.restoreVersion path — composer.history.restoreEntry() restores with no confirm and no safety save from two places. And 'pages, styles and brand settings' understates the blast radius: importProject replaces EVERY project setting (analytics, integrations, seo, publishing, customCode) and the CMS bindings.
evidence: Unconfirmed path: ActivityView.tsx:534 -> :369/:384 and HistoryTab.tsx:197 both call composer.history.restoreEntry(id) directly. Scope: Composer.ts:576 `applyProjectSettings(this.projectSettings, data.settings ?? {})` over ProjectSettings (shared/types/project.ts:258-279 = analytics, integrations, seo, publishing, customCode ...); Composer.ts:571-575 `if (data.cmsBindings) { this.cms.bindings.import(...) }`. 'Brand' is only designTokens/designPresets (rail/tabsConfig.ts:178). The three untouched stores ARE separate DBs and are genuinely untouched: aquibra-components (ComponentStorage.ts:15), aquibra-cms (CollectionStorage.ts:13), aquibra-media (IndexedDBAdapter.ts:14); exportProject hardcodes assets: [] (Composer.ts:616). The safety save IS taken and a throw aborts the restore (VersionTimelineManager.ts:290-299).
fix: Restore from the Saves list always confirms and always saves the current state as a version first — if that save fails, the restore is abandoned. It replaces pages, styles, every project setting (brand tokens, SEO, analytics, custom code) and the element→content bindings; the content records themselves, media and saved components are untouched. (Restoring from the activity list or the scrubber does neither.)

what: Layers hidden caption appended with 'Dimming is not undoable — ⌘Z skips it — and it is stored in this browser only, so a collaborator does not see it.'
finding: 'Skips it' understates what happens and is inferred rather than observed. ⌘Z is wired straight to composer.history.undo(), so it does not no-op — it pops the previous DOCUMENT edit, silently reverting real work while the dim stays on.
evidence: useLayerActions.ts:127-137 toggleVisibility calls setHiddenIds only and stamps data-hidden at :140-146; no composer.beginTransaction (contrast :211-213 deleteLayer, :222-224 duplicateLayer). useEditorShortcuts.ts:156 binds ⌘Z to composer.history.undo(). LAYER_VISIBILITY_TOGGLED is declared at events.ts:78 with an `undo: () => void` payload at :822 and appears nowhere else in src. 45% opacity IS real (layers-v2.css:56). Storage key shape confirmed (layersPersistence.ts:22).
fix: Hidden is not deleted. 45% opacity, keeps its place in the tree. Dimming opens no undo step, so ⌘Z undoes your previous edit instead and the dim stays on — and it is stored in this browser only, so a collaborator does not see it.

what: History activity caption, cap sentence appended: '...so a named version is the only thing that survives a long session.'
finding: The exclusivity is false. Auto-saves persist identically to named ones — same IndexedDB store, same server mirror — they are merely capped at 50 and pruned oldest-first. What a named version uniquely survives is the prune, not the session.
evidence: VersionHistoryStorage.ts:57-82 writeVersion writes every version to IndexedDB 'aquibra-versions' regardless of isAutoCheckpoint, plus versionSync.ts mirrorVersionCreate(version, isAuto). Everything else in the string is TRUE and measured: ActivityView.tsx:131 -> useHistoryState.ts:46 -> HistoryManager.ts:659 buildHistoryDisplayEntries(this.undoStack); HistoryManager.ts:156-160 resets both stacks on PROJECT_LOADED and HistoryFormatter.ts:21 skips index 0 so the list is empty; grep for localStorage|indexedDB|sessionStorage over HistoryManager.ts/HistoryFormatter.ts/historyTypes.ts returns zero; config.ts:108 HISTORY_MAX_SIZE: 100 with HistoryManager.ts:614 `this.undoStack.shift()`; HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING (events.ts:133) has exactly one occurrence in all of packages/editor/src — its own declaration.
fix: ...so a named version is the only thing guaranteed to survive a long session.

what: Compare side-by-side caption rewritten to '...Each pane is a sandboxed frame and they scroll separately — the labels carry the asymmetry, not colour.'
finding: 'They scroll separately' asserts a behaviour nobody measured. What is verified is the absence of sync code, which is not the same statement — whether either frame scrolls at all depends on the customer page's own CSS inside a srcDoc iframe. The caption also frames Compare as two modes; there are three.
evidence: ApprovedCompareView.tsx:92 `<iframe title="compare" sandbox="" srcDoc={page.html} className={className} />` is the single constructor for both split panes (:265,:270) and both overlay frames (:233,:238); grep for postMessage|useRef|onScroll|scrollTop|contentWindow returns zero hits, so nothing syncs them — but nothing measures them either. Labels ARE identical muted uppercase with no green (:64-66 PANE_LABEL, applied at :264 and :267). Third mode: :47 `type Mode = 'split' | 'overlay' | 'list'`, three buttons at :149-159 including 'List'. The overlay caption 172:10 is fully TRUE — :233 approved frame beneath, :237 the CURRENT frame wrapped in `style={{ opacity: overlayOpacity }}`, slider 0-100 step 2 at :248-256.
fix: Two independent panes. Left is the approved snapshot, right is the site as it is now. Each pane is a sandboxed frame and nothing syncs them — the labels carry the asymmetry, not colour. (A third mode, List, shows the same comparison as rows.)
